sentences.text: The present Appeal is filed at the instance of original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 11.12.2018, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vadodara in Motor Accident Claims Petition No. 715 of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined 2004 . By the said impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellant holding them entitled to total amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.
3,38,400/- with interest @ 9% from the date of filing of the claim petition till its actual realisation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Petition No. 715 of NEUTRAL
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The respondents herein-original opponents are held jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid amount of compensation.
4. This Court vide order dated 15.2.2023, noticing the grounds raised in the Appeal had admitted the Appeal and issued Notice for final hearing.
5. Despite service of Notice upon respondent No.1, no appearance has been entered on his behalf.
6. Learned advocate appearing for the appellant at the outset, has submitted that the learned Tribunal committed error in assessing the income of the appellant as Rs. 9000/- per month.

According to learned advocate, cogent material has been brought on record to indicate that the appellant was engaged as a Civil Engineer in a construction Company and was earning monthly salary of Rs. 10,000/- .
The owner of the aforesaid construction- company has been examined in this regard at Exh. 33.

Thus, according to learned advocate the Tribunal ought to have accepted the amount of Rs. 10,000/- as the income of the deceased as evident from the salary certificate produced on record at Exh. 34, however, the Tribunal while considering the aforesaid documents has assessed the income of the deceased on lower side to the extent of Rs. 9000/- only while considering that 10% of the aforesaid amount i.e Rs. 1000/- was required to be deducted NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined towards the tax.

Learned advocate had submitted that the Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact that no evidence worth has been brought on record to indicate that the income tax was required to be deducted towards his aforesaid earning.

He has further invited my attention to the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and has submitted that no contradictory material worth has been pointed out by the respondent-Insurance Company against the aforesaid material being brought on record.
He has therefore, urged this Court to consider the income of the appellant as Rs. 10,000/- per month.
6.1 Learned advocate had further submitted that the actual loss of income is also required to be reconsidered once the income of the appellant is considered as Rs. 10,000/- per month.
The attention of this Court was also invited to the nature of the injuries sustained by the appellant.

It is submitted that the appellant had sustained serious fracture injuries and considering the duration of treatment as indoor as well as outdoor patient, the Tribunal ought to have considered an amount of Rs. 50,000/- towards pain, shock and suffering.

sentences.text:
As regards the amount of compensation awarded towards medical expenses is concerned,
learned advocate had invited my attention to the medical bills produced on record.

While referring to the aforesaid documents produced on record at mark 23/7, learned advocate had urged this Court to reconsider and enhance the amount of compensation towards medical expenses from Rs. 3000/-
to Rs. 53,000/-.

6.3 Lastly, learned advocate has urged this Court to enhance the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined amount of compensation towards special diet and attendant charges from Rs. 5000/- to Rs. 10,000/- in the facts of the case.
By making aforesaid submissions learned advocate has urged this Court to enhance the total amount of compensation from Rs. 3,38,400/- to Rs. 4,19,000/-.
7. Learned advocate appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company has vehemently opposed to the aforesaid submissions made by learned advocate for the appellant.

Learned advocate has mainly relied upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and has submitted that considering the fact that the appellant was earning Rs. 10,000/- per month and the income tax prevalent at the relevant point of time, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 10% towards the income tax to be borne by the appellant, as against the income claimed.

Learned advocate had further submitted that looking to the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant the Court may consider their prayer for enhancement under the head of pain, shock and suffering.
However, he has objected to the amount to the tune of Rs. 1 lakh being prayed for by the appellant.

As regards the submissions made by learned advocate for enhancement of the amount of compensation to the tune of Rs. 53,000/-
towards medical expenses is concerned, learned advocate had drawn my attention to the aforesaid document on record and has submitted that in absence of any original document being proved on record or any witness being examined, the Tribunal has rightly accepted the objection raised by learned advocate for the Insurance and has rightly not admitted it as an evidence.

He has therefore,
submitted that the Tribunal has rightly awarded an amount of Rs. 3000/- towards medical expenses.

As regards submissions made by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined learned advocate for the amount of compensation towards special diet and attendant charges and transport expenses are concerned.
Learned advocate has urged this Court to consider just and reasonable amount of compensation towards the same.
8. I have heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and have examined their arguments in light of the evidence brought on record.

The submissions made by learned advocate for the appellant with regard to income being assessed on the lower side is concerned, I have considered the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal in this regard.
8.1
It transpires on record that the applicant-claimant was engaged as a Civil Engineer in a private construction company.
The owner of the construction company has been examined by him as witness at Exh. 33.
The salary certificate has been brought on record at Exh. 34.
Thus the fact that the claimant was earning Rs. 10,000/- per month has been established by the claimant on record.

This brings me to the issue of deduction of 10% of the aforesaid income as deducted by the Tribunal towards the income tax is concerned, upon careful examination of the findings and reasons assigned by Tribunal while applying 10% deduction towards income tax is concerned, no evidence worth in Arvindbhai Ashalal Shah vs Dilipbhai Gordhanbhai Patel on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162098811/
3 this regard has been brought on record.

sentences.text: 8.2. The Tribunal merely on assumption and presumptions has arrived at a finding that since the claimant was earning the income of Rs. 10,000/- per month considering the bracket of income and the rate of income tax prevailing at the relevant point has applied 10% deduction.

The aforesaid approach of Tribunal is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined erroneous as against settled proposition, which calls for interference by this Court in the present appeal.
8.3 The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Vimal Kanwar and Ors. Vs. Kishore Dan and Ors.

entities.text: Vimal Kanwar and Ors. Vs. Kishore Dan and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(2013) 7 SCC 476 has held as under:
22.
In the present case, none of the respondents brought to the notice of the Court that the income-tax payable by the deceased Sajjan Singh was not deducted at source by the employer- State Government.

No such statement was made by Ram Avtar Parikh, PW-2 an employee of Public Works Department of the State Government who placed on record the Last Pay Certificate and the Service Book of the deceased.
The Tribunal or the High Court on perusal of the Last Pay Certificate, have not noticed that the income-tax on the estimated income of the employee was not deducted from the salary of the employee during the said month or Financial Year.

In absence of such evidence, it is presumed that the salary paid to the deceased Sajjan Singh as per Last Pay Certificate was paid in accordance with law i.e. by deducting the income-tax on the estimated income of the deceased Sajjan Singh for that month or the Financial Year.
The appellants have specifically stated that Assessment Year applicable in the instant case is 1997-98 and not 1996-97 as held by the High Court.
They have also taken specific plea that for the Assessment Year 1997-98 the rate of tax on income more than 40,000/- and upto Rs.60,000/- was 15% and not 20% as held by the High Court.
The aforesaid fact has not been disputed by the respondents.

23. In view of the finding as recorded above and the provisions of the Income-tax Act,
1961, as discussed, we hold that the High Court was wrong in deducting 20% from the salary of the deceased towards income-tax, for calculating the compensation.

As per law, the presumption will be that employer-State Government at the time of payment of salary deducted income- tax on the estimated income of the deceased employee from the salary and in absence of any evidence, we hold that the salary as shown in the Last Pay Certificate at Rs.8,920/- should be accepted which if rounded off comes to Rs.9,000/- for calculating the compensation payable to the dependent(s).
24. The fourth issue is "whether the compensation awarded to the appellants is just and proper."
For determination of this issue, it is required to determine the percentage of increase in income to be made towards prospects of advancement in future career and revision of pay.

In General Manager, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation, Trivandrum v. Susamma Thomas (1994) 2 SCC 176 this Court noticed the age and income of the deceased for determination of future prospects of Arvindbhai Ashalal Shah vs Dilipbhai Gordhanbhai Patel on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162098811/
4 advancement in life NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/07/2025 undefined and career.

sentences.text:
The Court held as follows:
"19.
In the present case the deceased was 39 years of age.
His income was Rs 1032 per month.
Of course, the future prospects of advancement in life and career should also be sounded in terms of money to augment the multiplicand.

While the chance of the multiplier is determined by two factors, namely, the rate of interest appropriate to a stable economy and the age of the deceased or of the claimant whichever is higher,
the ascertainment of the multiplicand is a more difficult exercise.
Indeed, many factors have to be put into the scales to evaluate the contingencies of the future.
All contingencies of the future need not necessarily be baneful.
The deceased person in this case had a more or less stable job.

It will not be inappropriate to take a reasonably liberal view of the prospects of the future and in estimating the gross income it will be unreasonable to estimate the loss of dependency on the present actual income of Rs 1032 per month.

We think, having regard to the prospects of advancement in the future career, respecting which there is evidence on record, we will not be in error in making a higher estimate of monthly income at Rs 2000 as the gross income."
25.

In New India Assurance Co.Ltd. v. Gopali & ors. reported in AIR 2012 SC 3381 this Court noticed that the High Court determined the compensation by granting 100% increase in the income of the deceased.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd. v. Gopali & ors. reported in AIR 2012 SC 3381
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Taking into consideration the fact that in the normal course, the deceased would have served for 22 years and during that period his salary would have certainly doubled, this Court,
upheld the judgment of the High Court.
8.4 The aforesaid legal principles squarely applies to the present case.

In the opinion of this Court,
the Tribunal committed serious error in considering the deduction of Rs 1000/- towards the income tax.
In absence of any cogent evidence being brought on record in this regard.
Hence this Court is inclined to accept the submissions of learned advocate for the appellant to consider the income of claimant as Rs. 10,000/- per month.

8.5 Having held so, the loss sustained towards actual loss towards the income or the period during which the claimant was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined hospitalized and was under treatment is also required to be re- considered.

Though the learned advocate for the appellant has prayed for the actual loss of income to be considered for more than 2 months, in absence of any evidence being brought on record, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the aforesaid finding of the Tribunal, however, considering the fact that income of the claimant is considered to be Rs.,10,000/- per month.
The actual loss of income is reconsidered and is enhanced from Rs. 18,000/- to Rs. 20,000/-.

8.6 As regards the submissions made by learned advocate for adopting of multiplier and permanent partial disability sustained by the original claimant is concerned, in absence of any challenge being made by the appellant and considering the findings and reasons assigned by the learned Tribunal,
this Court finds that in the facts of the case noticing the age of the claimant as 61 years, the Tribunal Arvindbhai Ashalal Shah vs Dilipbhai Gordhanbhai Patel on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162098811/
5 has rightly applied the multiplier of 7 in light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and Ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation Ors. (2009) ACJ 1298, 8.7

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the permanent partial disability sustained by the claimant is concerned, indisputably the purshis has been filed at Exh. 29 whereby the respective parties have agreed to treat permanent partial disability of the claimant to be 40% of body as a whole in absence of any medical expert being examined in this regard by the claimant, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the aforesaid findings treating the permanent partial disability of 40% of body as a whole.

Hence, the future prospective loss of the income of the claimant is reconsidered as Rs.10,000/- multiplied by 12 multiplied by 7 multiplied by 40% which comes to Rs.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined 3,36,000/-.
Thus, the amount of future loss of income is enhanced from Rs. 3,02,400/- to Rs. 3,36,000/-.

8.8 As regards the submission made by learned advocate for the amount of compensation towards pain, shock and suffering is concerned noticing the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant, it is evident that the appellant has sustained sciatic nerve palsy and left hip degenerated charges which has led him to problem in walking for life long and considering the fact that the age of the claimant was 61 years at the time of occurrence of the accident, this Court is inclined to accept the aforesaid submissions of learned advocate for the appellant.

The amount of compensation towards pain,
shock and suffering is therefore reconsidered and enhanced from Rs. 10,000/- to Rs. 50,000/-.
As regards the enhancement sought for under the head of special diet, attendant charges and transportation expenses are concerned, the same is enhanced from Rs. 5000/- to Rs. 10,000/-.

8.9 Noticing the fact that the medical bills produced on record does not bear the endorsement of any medical officer of the concerned hospital where the claimant had taken treatment, in the opinion of this Court in absence of any witness being examined in this regard the Tribunal has rightly not accepted it as an evidence.
Hence, the prayer for enhancement of amount of compensation towards medical expenses is not entertained.

9. For the forgoing reasons, the amount of compensation is reconsidered as under :

X Prospective -   Total 1,08,000/- 
 X 40% of disability 40% 
 Total 43,200/- 
 Total 3,02,400/- 
 2. Actual loss of income 18,000/-

6  2 month  3. Pain shock suffering 10,000/- 
 4. Special diet 5,000/- 
 Transportation  Attendant charges  5. Loss amenities  6. Medical expenses 3,000/- 
 7. Future Medical  Total 3,38,400/- 
 Negligence   Grand Total   Awarded Amount  Enhanced Amount  Rate of Interest  10.
Hence, this First Appeal is allowed.
The appel claimant is held entitled to total amount of compensation to the tune of Rs. 4,19,000/-.

Since the Tribunal by impugned judgment and award has considered compensation of Rs. 3,38,400/-, the appellant is held entitled to enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs. 80,600/-( Rs 4,19,000 minus Rs. 3,38,400/-).

The respondents-original opponent being held jointly and severally liable to pay the amount of compensation, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3527/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined it is directed that respondent shall deposit the aforesaid amount of compensation with the concerned Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
On the deposit of the aforesaid awarded amount the Tribunal is at liberty to release and disburse the aforesaid entire awarded amount in favour of the claimant subject to due verification.
The Tribunal shall strictly adhere to the guidelines of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard.
11. The First Appeal stands allowed to the aforesaid extent.
R and P to be send back to the concerned Court forthwith.
